commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): auto-classify job title families, deterministic-first with LLM fallback

The Job titles edit UI required a human to manually type a family for
every title, defaulting to a bare "Unclassified" string sitting in the
edit box -- friction on a 290-title backlog (84% still unclassified),
and confusing on its own (a free-text field pre-filled with the literal
word "Unclassified" reads as something broken, not as "nothing set
yet"). This turn: classify it automatically instead.

classify_job_title_family (app/understanding/taxonomy/
title_family_classifier.py) tries a keyword ruleset first -- IT staffing
titles are extremely repetitive ("<Tech> Developer", "SAP <Module>
Consultant", "<Domain> Business Analyst") -- and only calls the LLM
(same LiteLLM gateway every other Hermes AI capability uses, same
pattern as generate_skill_description) for the genuine minority a
keyword can't place. Measured against the real 290-title backlog: 243
(84%) classify deterministically, with zero model calls; the remaining
47 get a sensible LLM classification (verified: "UKG Kronos Consultant"
-> HCM, "Network Manager" -> Infrastructure). A title neither path can
place stays exactly as Unclassified as before -- never a fabricated
guess.

Wired into three places:
- approve_taxonomy_candidate: approving a job_title candidate without
  an explicit family (the review page's normal path) now auto-classifies
  instead of defaulting to "Unclassified" -- new titles stop adding to
  the backlog instead of only ever growing it.
- POST /taxonomy/job-titles/auto-classify: one-shot bulk pass over
  every currently-Unclassified title, for clearing the existing backlog.
- POST /taxonomy/job-titles/suggest-family: per-title preview for the
  edit page's "Suggest" button -- classifies without writing, so a
  reviewer can see it and still override before saving.

JobTitlesTaxonomyPage.tsx: the free-text-with-datalist family field
(confusing, per the report) is now a plain <select> of known families
plus a "Suggest" button that fills it from the classifier. A header
button runs the bulk auto-classify pass and reports how many got
placed vs. still need a human.

New coverage: common title patterns classify deterministically; a
title neither path can place stays cleanly Unclassified with no LLM
key configured; approving without an explicit family auto-classifies,
an explicit family still overrides it; suggest previews without adding
a title; bulk auto-classify places every deterministic hit and leaves
genuine misses alone. Full regression suite (18 checks, 6 new) green
against a fresh schema and rebuilt image; frontend type-checks and
builds clean.
